# Load packages
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(igraph)
library(NBZIMM)
library(lme4)
library(SpiecEasi)
library(LIMON)
library(ggeffects)
library(car)
library(phyloseq)
library(metagMisc)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Prep data
## Load metadata
```{r}
# load metadata
outdir <- here("data", "ML")
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE,
           showWarnings = FALSE)

# load metadata
psdir <- here("data", "phyloseq")
ps_ASVs <- readRDS(file = file.path(psdir, 'ps_css.rds'))

maasdir <- here("data", "MaasLin2")

input_metadata <- data.frame(ps_ASVs@sam_data) %>%
  mutate(sex = as.factor(Infant_gender)) %>%
  mutate(Residency_status = as.factor(case_when(Residency_status == 1 ~ 0,
                                         Residency_status == 2 ~ 1)))

rownames(input_metadata) <- input_metadata$SampleID

input_metadata <- input_metadata %>%
  dplyr::select(c("sex", "gest_week_s", "age_s", "bmi_s", "Residency_status", "parity_s", "run_accession", "SampleID")) #%>%
  # mutate(Time = 1)

#sample_data(ps_filtered) <- metadata
```

# Model 1 - covariates only
```{r}
covariate_model <- input_metadata %>%
  dplyr::select(c("sex", "gest_week_s", "age_s", "bmi_s", "Residency_status", "parity_s"))

ncol(covariate_model)

write.csv(covariate_model, file = file.path(outdir, "model1_covariates.csv"))
```

# Model 2 - microbes + covariates
```{r}
# load phyloseq object
ps.f <- readRDS(file = file.path(psdir, 'ps_css.rds'))

# Extract sample names from the phyloseq object
sample_ids <- sample_names(ps.f)
input_metadata <- input_metadata[input_metadata$run_accession %in% sample_ids, ]
```

## use sex & sex*ega sig taxa
### read in files
```{r}
sex_microbes <- read.csv(file.path(maasdir, "asvs_zinb", "sex_ega_sig_microbes.csv"), row.names = 1)
```

### prep data
```{r}
sig_sex_taxa <- sex_microbes %>%
  filter(metadata %in% c("fetal_sex_binary", "sex_x_ega"))

ps_ml <- prune_taxa(sig_sex_taxa$feature, ps.f)

# Extract metadata and set new sample names from "SampleID" column
sample_data(ps_ml)$SampleID <- as.character(sample_data(ps_ml)$SampleID)  # Ensure SampleID is character
sample_names(ps_ml) <- sample_data(ps_ml)$SampleID

ps_ml
```

```{r}
ml_asvs <- data.frame(otu_table(ps_ml))

# Replace zeros with a small pseudocount
pseudocount <- min(ml_asvs[ml_asvs > 0]) / 2
ml_asvs[ml_asvs == 0] <- pseudocount

# CLR transform (apply by row)
clr_counts <- apply(ml_asvs, 1, compositions::clr)

# Convert back to data frame (optional)
clr_counts <- as.data.frame(clr_counts)

clr_counts$SampleID <- rownames(clr_counts)

ncol(clr_counts)
```


```{r}
# read in covariate model
#covariate_model <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model1_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)

covariate_model$SampleID <- rownames(covariate_model)

# Ensure both datasets have a common column for merging (e.g., "SampleID")
clr_counts <- clr_counts %>%
  full_join(covariate_model, by = "SampleID")

rownames(clr_counts) <- clr_counts$SampleID

clr_counts <- clr_counts %>%
  dplyr::select(-SampleID)

write.csv(clr_counts, file = file.path(outdir, "model2_asvs_covariates.csv"))
```

# Model 3 - kegg + covariates
## CLR transforming using compositions
```{r}
## To keep dataset transformations consistent for enzymes and ASVs, we will subset the raw picrust data to include only features of interest and then clr transform that

# load KO file
picrust.kegg <- read.csv(file = here("data", "picrust2", "picrust_output_css_all",
                                     "KO_metagenome_out",
                                     "pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv.gz"),
                         sep = "\t", row.names = 1)

sex_kegg <- read.csv(file = here("data/MaasLin2/picrust2_output_css_all",
                                    "KEGG",
                                    "significant_results.tsv"),
                        sep = "\t")

sig_sex_kegg <- sex_kegg %>%
  filter(metadata %in% c("fetal_sex_binary", "sex_x_ega"))

selected_kegg_ids <- sig_sex_kegg$feature

css_filtered <- data.frame(t(picrust.kegg))
# Filter the phyloseq object to keep only the top taxa
css_filtered <- css_filtered[ ,selected_kegg_ids]

# transpose css_filtered so KEGGs are rows and samples are columns
#css_filtered <- t(css_filtered)

# Match current rownames to metadata
idx <- match(
  rownames(css_filtered),
  input_metadata$run_accession
)

# Check for unmatched samples
if (any(is.na(idx))) {
  stop(
    "Some run_accession values were not found in input_metadata: ",
    paste(
      rownames(css_filtered)[is.na(idx)],
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}

# Replace rownames with SampleID
rownames(css_filtered) <- input_metadata$SampleID[idx]

head(rownames(css_filtered))

anyDuplicated(input_metadata$run_accession)
anyDuplicated(input_metadata$SampleID)

# Replace zeros with a small pseudocount
pseudocount <- min(css_filtered[css_filtered > 0]) / 2
css_filtered[css_filtered == 0] <- pseudocount

# CLR transform (apply by row)
clr_counts <- apply(css_filtered, 1, compositions::clr)

# Convert back to data frame (optional)
clr_counts <- as.data.frame(t(clr_counts))

clr_counts$SampleID <- rownames(clr_counts)

ncol(clr_counts)

# read in covariate model
covariate_model <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model1_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)

covariate_model$SampleID <- rownames(covariate_model)

# Ensure both datasets have a common column for merging (e.g., "SampleID")
clr_counts <- clr_counts %>%
  left_join(covariate_model, by = "SampleID")

rownames(clr_counts) <- clr_counts$SampleID

clr_counts <- clr_counts %>%
  dplyr::select(-SampleID)

write.csv(clr_counts, file = file.path(outdir, "model3_kegg_covariates.csv"))
```

# Model 6 - combine microbes & kegg
## Uncorrected counts
```{r}
asvs <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model2_asvs_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)
keggs <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model3_enzymes_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)

asvs <- asvs[,!(colnames(asvs) %in% c("sex", "gest_week_s", "age_s", "bmi_s", "Residency_status", "parity_s"))]


asvs$SampleID <- rownames(asvs)

keggs$SampleID <- rownames(keggs)

# Merge dataframes by "SampleID" and keep only one "sex" column
combined_df <- full_join(asvs, keggs, by = "SampleID") %>%
  # dplyr::rename(sex = sex.y) %>%       # Rename "sex.x" back to "sex"
  # dplyr::select(-sex.x) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "SampleID")

# View the merged dataframe
head(combined_df)

write.csv(combined_df, file = file.path(outdir, "model6_asvs_kegg_combined.csv"))
```

# Model 9 - combine microbes, keggs, pathways
## Uncorrected counts
```{r}
asvs <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model2_asvs_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)
keggs <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model3_enzymes_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)
pathways <- read.csv(file = here("data/ML/model5_pathways_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)

asvs <- asvs[,!(colnames(asvs) %in% c("sex", "gest_week_s", "age_s", "bmi_s", "Residency_status", "parity_s"))]
keggs <- keggs[,!(colnames(keggs) %in% c("sex", "gest_week_s", "age_s", "bmi_s", "Residency_status", "parity_s"))]

asvs$SampleID <- rownames(asvs)

keggs$SampleID <- rownames(keggs)

pathways$SampleID <- rownames(pathways)

# Merge dataframes by "SampleID" and keep only one "sex" column
combined_df <- asvs %>%
  full_join(keggs, by = "SampleID") %>%
  full_join(pathways, by = "SampleID") %>%
  # dplyr::rename(sex = sex.y) %>%       # Rename "sex.x" back to "sex"
  # dplyr::select(-sex.x) %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "SampleID")

# View the merged dataframe
head(combined_df)

write.csv(combined_df, file = file.path(outdir, "model9_asvs_kegg_pathways_combined.csv"))
```
